title: Degenerates at Playwrights Horizons by Else Went #degenerates #playwr...
transcript: The kids are far from alright in this fascinating new play by Else Went at Playrights Horizons. I thought, based on the marketing, that it was going to be about a group of incels hopelessly stuck in the manosphere. And that's kind of what it seems like at first, but as it chugs along, a much more layered story emerges — one that's delicate, sad and hopeful all at the same time. The two primary characters in this play spend most of it in their own rooms, conversing over voice chat. When they decide to meet IRL, it's a bewildering experience and it kind of reconstructs their entire worldviews and their identities. It's a story about loneliness and the complex nature of trying to break that loneliness. Two things can be true — we can face rejections that thrust loneliness upon us, and we can isolate ourselves further because it's comfortable that way. This methodically slow and sizzling piece drops you into an existence with these characters that's so insular, it almost feels like a simulation, aided by the occasional audio descriptions, narrations and stage directions delivered over the God mic. A lot of the choices behind the structure and direction of this play seem really odd until they come together in a riveting second act. I think they're still calibrating some of the pacing and the tone of the production, but it's already quite compelling. It'll make you think, reflect, and certainly wanna touch grass. With that, another program for my collection.
classificationReason: Creator shares a first-hand, opinionated review of Degenerates at Playwrights Horizons, discussing plot, direction, and structure with clear personal assessment.
